title: The Blaschka Object Network — Dealer Archive Register
scope: Archival survival of the three documented commercial dealers/distributors of Blaschka marine-invertebrate models: Henry Augustus Ward / Ward's Natural Science Establishment, Robert Damon / Robert Ferris Damon, and Václav Frič. The register distinguishes intact business archives from dispersed dealer correspondence preserved by the Blaschka workshop, customers, museums and later manuscript collections.
methodological_guard: A museum holding objects bought from a dealer is not treated as a dealer archive unless a named correspondence, acquisition, accounts or business-record series can be identified. 'No dedicated corporate fonds identified' means only that this project pass has not located one; it is not a claim that no such records survive anywhere. Dealer correspondence is kept distinct from Blaschka-specific transaction evidence until item content establishes the link.

status_vocabulary.intact_business_archive: A named personal/business archive survives as a collection of record or corporate archive.
status_vocabulary.distributed_business_correspondence: No dedicated corporate fonds has been identified in this pass; business evidence survives across workshop and customer-side archives.
status_vocabulary.direct_blaschka_dealer_evidence: The source explicitly concerns Blaschka models, their catalogue, order, payment, packing, shipment or agency arrangement.
status_vocabulary.receiving_side_dealer_file: Customer or museum records explicitly document transactions with the dealer but require item-level checking for Blaschka content.
status_vocabulary.general_dealer_business_context: Dealer correspondence demonstrating the firm's wider commercial practice; useful for network reconstruction but not evidence for a Blaschka transaction by itself.
status_vocabulary.post_blaschka_business_context: Dealer correspondence after marine-model production ended; useful for the firm's wider commercial history but not evidence for a Blaschka transaction by itself.

research_value: dealer-side comparison with Dresden workshop accounts

blaschka_specific_evidence.note: Dyer explicitly states that historical records of purchase in the Henry Augustus Ward papers were examined together with Leopold Blaschka's business notebooks and correspondence to reconstruct North-American receipt and distribution.
A copy is preserved in A.W23 and is a principal commercial concordance for the Blaschka marine-model series.

critical_gaps: A dedicated Damon firm archive, order book or invoice series has not been located in this pass.
The dealer's incoming side of the Blaschka agency correspondence remains substantially less visible than the workshop's outgoing drafts.
Customer-side Damon files need item-level inspection for Blaschka catalogue lists, prices, packing, remittances and damage reports.

dealers.name: Václav Frič / V. Frič natural-history and teaching-aids business
dealers.business_history_guard: The firm was founded in 1861, continued under Jaromír Frič after Václav Frič, and ended in 1959. The National Museum in Prague received remaining natural-history stock; this transfer of stock is not treated as proof that a complete company paper archive was transferred.

workshop_side_counterpart.repository: Rakow Research Library, Corning Museum of Glass
workshop_side_counterpart.series: Blaschka business notebooks and letter drafts
workshop_side_counterpart.notable_item: 8 November 1884 draft to Václav Frič concerning a commercial shipment and four glass models sent as a gift to the Prague museum
workshop_side_counterpart.research_value: Reseller relations, shipment composition, gifts, catalogue commerce and workshop-side dealer correspondence.

distributed_archival_witnesses.collection: Trustee Minutes, Outward Letter Books and purchase-of-specimens correspondence
distributed_archival_witnesses.evidence: The museum's archival reconstruction found the 1879 instruction to Frič to obtain Blaschka glass invertebrates and later correspondence about three mixed consignments.

distributed_archival_witnesses.collection: National Museum registry and Antonín Frič personal fonds
distributed_archival_witnesses.coverage: institutional records of the National Museum plus Antonín Frič's written estate
distributed_archival_witnesses.evidence: Published reconstruction joins the 8 November 1884 workshop draft to a National Museum accession record for Frič's delivery of four Blaschka models. The archive also preserves the personal fonds of Antonín Frič, a major museum-side natural-history actor.
distributed_archival_witnesses.blaschka_guard: Antonín Frič's fonds is distinct from the commercial papers of Václav Frič's firm; no complete V. Frič corporate archive is inferred.

distributed_archival_witnesses.coverage: Erwerbungen beim Naturalienhändler V. Fric (Prag), 1864-1869 and 1883
distributed_archival_witnesses.blaschka_guard: The finding aid proves a dedicated Frič acquisition file at the receiving institution, not that it contains Blaschka models.

distributed_archival_witnesses.repository: Archivo del Museo Nacional de Ciencias Naturales, CSIC, Madrid
distributed_archival_witnesses.collection: Personal Científico Ignacio Bolívar y Urrutia — Correspondencia. Entidades
distributed_archival_witnesses.coverage: Václav Frič letter from Prague to Ignacio Bolívar, 18 July 1885, offering insects for purchase
distributed_archival_witnesses.evidence: The fully catalogued manuscript explicitly identifies V. Frič. Lehrmittel und Naturalien-Handlung and is digitally available through Simurg.
distributed_archival_witnesses.blaschka_guard: Not a Blaschka transaction; direct evidence of Frič's international dealer correspondence in the same commercial period.

distributed_archival_witnesses.coverage: three items from V. Fric, Prague, 1905
distributed_archival_witnesses.blaschka_guard: Post-production business context only unless item content establishes an earlier collection link.

critical_gaps: A dedicated V. Frič company correspondence/account archive has not been identified in this pass.
The relationship between surviving company stock transferred to the National Museum in 1959 and surviving business papers remains unresolved.
Dealer-side order books, invoices and customer ledgers would be the decisive source for reconstructing the Austria-Hungary network at scale.

network_observation: The archival asymmetry is itself significant. Ward has an identifiable personal and corporate archive. Damon and Frič currently have to be reconstructed from the Blaschka workshop archive plus customer-side correspondence, museum acquisition files and scattered manuscript collections. The distribution system therefore survives in the same fragmented form as the objects it moved: concentrated at one dealer, institutionally dispersed at the others.
